content.comment_body: Hello, I have a project where I need to generate a pulse output to energize a solenoid valve for a configurable duration between 60ms and 200ms. This is not PWM; the pulse occurs just once in a specified time interval (minutes/hours). Is it possible to achieve this using [product_name] hardware/software, or should I consider upgrading to [version_no]? I've read online that [product_name] may not support such fast operations, but perhaps someone has experience with this type of application? Thank you in advance. [user_name]

How do you intend the impulse to be output? With a relay or transistor output? If using a transistor output, what is the load's current consumption? Technically, it is feasible to generate pulses ranging from 60 to 200 ms.

I doubt that a relay output can switch this quickly, so a transistor output is probably best. Regarding the load, I'm not sure of the exact value, but it is meant to control an SSR with a response time of 10 ms (from Phoenix Contact).

Sorry if my question about relay output was unclear. I'm not familiar with the questioner's technical level. With [product_name], the pulse duration can be set in 10 ms increments (e.g., 10ms, 20ms, 30ms, etc.). I asked about the load because transistor outputs can handle up to 0.3 A maximum.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum participants are discussing whether [product_name] hardware and software can reliably produce one-off short output pulses (60–200 ms) through transistor outputs, especially for activating a solenoid valve via an SSR. There is concern about the speed, timing resolution, and whether [product_name] hardware is suitable for such precise and fast tasks, as well as uncertainty about the limitations of different output types.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects [product_name] to generate accurate single output pulses between 60 and 200 milliseconds using transistor outputs and to offer adequate timing precision and output current capability for controlling their application.
